key_results: Unannealed PbSc₀.₅Ta₀.₅O₃ (S₁₁₁~0.6) achieves ΔTⱼ~3.1 K vs. 4.0 K for annealed (S₁₁₁~0.9–0.96); performance reduction only 22.5% despite eliminating 42-day anneal
comments: Reduced latent heat offset by high-field electrocaloric effects in induced ferroelectric phase; eliminates expensive annealing without severely compromising performance; economically and environmentally beneficial.

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-field electrocaloric effects in induced ferroelectric phase compensate for reduced latent heat in unannealed samples
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 3.1 K achieved in unannealed material; only 22.5% performance loss vs. annealed reference

title: Electron dynamics in graphene irradiated by a quantum wave packet versus a classical point charge
task: Benchmarking quantum vs. classical descriptions of electron irradiation via backscattering in graphene
key_results: At ~400 eV: quantum wave packet yields finite backscattering while classical ensemble predicts vanishing; quantum yield remains finite at higher energies, gradually decreasing
comments: Unexpected regime where quantum-classical predictions diverge markedly; identifies targeted experimental energy window for validating computational models; guides 2D material nanofabrication design.

model_io.model: First-principles quantum-mechanical electron dynamics in graphene
inputs: electron description (quantum wave packet vs. classical ensemble)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum and classical electron descriptions diverge in backscattering predictions around 400 eV incident energy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: quantum wave packet yields finite backscattering while classical vanishes; provides benchmarking energy window

title: Navigating order-disorder family trees via group-subgroup transitions
task: Organizing ordered and disordered crystal structures via group-subgroup symmetry family trees
key_results: Many apparent novel ordered structures are ordered children of known disordered parents; symmetry-agnostic generative models 2–4× more prone to this; symmetry-constrained models avoid false novelty
comments: Practical framework for genuine novelty assessment in materials discovery; validated on A-Lab, ICSD, MP-20, Alex-MP-20, GNoME; impacts evaluation of generative models.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Symmetry-agnostic generative models produce more ordered-child false positives than symmetry-aware models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 2–4× higher false-novelty rate; order-disorder family trees essential for genuine discovery evaluation

title: Super-resolution tactile sensing through geometric encoding in liquid-metal microchannels
task: Achieving super-resolution tactile sensing via geometry-encoded liquid-metal microchannels
key_results: 0.230 mm mean localization RMSE across three fabricated devices; super-resolution factor 58.3; force RMSE 0.043 N; 95.38% keyboard classification accuracy with only four resistive channels
comments: Kernel-based simulator enables noise-aware optimization without full FEM; hierarchical mixture-of-experts decoder jointly estimates position and force; thin, compliant form factor.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Geometric encoding of contact information into microchannel topology enables sub-millimeter localization from sparse readout
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 0.228 mm RMSE achieved (58.3× super-resolution) with only 4 channels; reproducible across independent devices

title: High-key-rate fully-passive quantum access network with thermal source
task: Demonstrating high-rate passive quantum access networks using continuous-variable QKD with thermal source
key_results: Four QNUs achieve average end-to-end secret key rate 12.82 Mbps per QNU (untrusted assumption); passive state preparation eliminates active modulation; point-to-multi-point topology matches classical access networks
comments: PSP-QPON extends passive state prep from point-to-point to networks; free-space and fiber hybrid channels; conservative untrusted assumption provides stringent security bound.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fully passive state preparation enables high-rate quantum access networks matching classical infrastructure topology
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 12.82 Mbps per QNU achievable with passive PSP; untrusted-assumption security bound rigorous

title: Thermal enhancement mechanisms in a heat exchanger installed with gear-ring turbulence promoters
task: Enhancing heat transfer in tubes using gear-shaped turbulators
key_results: Nusselt number increases 1.82–2.67×; friction factor rises 8.37–12.53×; peak thermal performance factor 1.16 at Re=6000, N=8, PR=2
comments: Trade-off between heat transfer enhancement and pressure drop penalty is substantial; GRI configuration with N=8 and PR=2 offers best thermal performance.

model_io.model: Turbulent flow in tube with gear-ring insert

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gear-shaped turbulators intensify fluid mixing and disrupt boundary layers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 1.82–2.67× Nusselt enhancement with significant pressure loss penalty

title: An initial investigation into a low-complexity adaptive transparency framework for hearables using spectral analysis and loudness control
task: Implementing adaptive transparency architecture for hearables using spectral analysis and loudness control
key_results: Proposed system shows lower peak-to-average ratio, improved transient handling, faster recovery, smoother loudness trajectories vs. three static baselines; ~9000 MAC operations per hop (hearable-compatible)
comments: Proof-of-concept framework; short-time energy and spectral centroid drive harsh-event detection; adaptive RMS limiter uses exponential moving average and percentile-based estimation, not validated psychoacoustic model; informal author-only perceptual evaluation on limited corpus—requires formal listener panel and larger dataset.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Content-aware filtering and statistically-driven loudness control reduce harshness and improve stability vs. static transparency
hypotheses.result: Indicative: lower peak-to-average ratio, faster recovery, smoother trajectories observed on limited test set; formal validation required

title: Mechanical and multi-radiation shielding performance of concrete optimized with activated carbon and silica fume
task: Optimizing multi-radiation shielding performance of concrete with activated carbon and silica fume
key_results: AC 2–4% by mass optimizes compressive strength; AC–SF hybrid mixtures achieve superior shielding; gamma-ray attenuation validated XCOM/MCNPX (deviation <7%); extended MCNPX to 15 MeV for Zeff, Neff, Zeq, ΣR predictions
comments: Optimal AC–SF mixture (2% AC + 10% SF) balances structural integrity and shielding; model validation enables high-energy predictions without expensive experiments.

model_io.model: Concrete mixture + MCNPX radiation transport simulator

hypotheses.hypothesis: AC–SF hybrid mixtures optimize both mechanical strength and multi-radiation shielding efficiency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 2% AC + 10% SF achieves best balance; MCNPX model validation (error <7%) enables high-energy extrapolation

title: All-dielectric TiO₂ and Poly-Si grating RGB color filters for CMOS image sensor
task: Designing all-dielectric RGB color filters for CMOS image sensors using TiO₂ and Poly-Si gratings
key_results: Peak transmittances: blue 83.3%, green 83.7%, red 79.01%; FWHM 70.9/96.1/91.6 nm (Q-factors 6.3/5.7/6.8); sRGB gamut coverage 21.6% vs. 14.7% baseline; mean CIEDE2000 2.48 on ColorChecker
comments: No metal in optical path eliminates Ohmic loss; Fano lineshape and leaky guided-mode resonance tuning via Si₃N₄/SiO₂ spacers; angle stability ±15–20°; CMOS-compatible excimer-laser annealing route proposed.

model_io.model: All-dielectric RGB grating filter set (TiO₂ blue, Poly-Si green/red)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Leaky guided-mode resonance tuning via spacer design enables high-transmission all-dielectric RGB filters
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 83%+ transmittance achieved; Fano-lineshape analysis validates coupled mode mechanism; sRGB coverage 21.6% vs. 14.7% dye-based baseline

title: Compact SWB monopole antenna with an SWB frequency selective surface for radiation performance enhancement
task: Enhancing SWB monopole antenna radiation performance with FSS backing layers
key_results: Operating bandwidth 2.9–48 GHz; peak gain 8.3 dBi; compact size 28×28×29.2 mm³ with 4×4 FSS array
comments: FSS sheets reflect backward radiation effectively; antenna geometry uses triangular and rectangular cuts for impedance matching and broadband response.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FSS backing improves antenna gain and directivity while maintaining broadband performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 4×4 FSS array achieves 8.3 dBi gain with 2.9–48 GHz bandwidth in compact form

title: Experimental and first-principles investigation of NO2 sensing behaviour in tetragonal ZrO2 nanoparticles
task: Characterizing NO₂ sensing behavior in tetragonal ZrO₂ nanoparticles via experiment and DFT
key_results: NO₂ response 87.5% at 200°C; response time 12 s, recovery 21 s; linear sensitivity 20–160 ppm; stable over 50 days; optical band gap 3.8 eV (DFT: 4.03 eV indirect)
comments: Mesoporous structure (3.49 nm pore diameter) enhances sensor performance; DFT density of states shows Zr 4d (CB) and O 2p (VB) dominance; adsorption-induced electronic modulation mechanism confirmed.

model_io.model: Tetragonal ZrO₂ nanoparticle thick-film sensor + DFT simulator

hypotheses.hypothesis: ZrO₂ mesoporous nanostructure with appropriate band gap enables sensitive NO₂ detection via adsorption-induced electronic modulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 87.5% response at 200°C; stability over 50 days; DFT density of states consistent with experimental optical properties

title: Surface adsorption and phase-selective electronic modulation of monolayer TaSe $$_2$$
task: Characterizing adsorbate-induced electronic structure modulation in monolayer TMD phases
key_results: K induces rigid band shift on both 1T/1H phases; CO and O₂ cause strong 1T shift via interfacial dipole but minimal 1H change; Fe causes spectral broadening without shift
comments: Reveals phase-selectivity of adsorbate interactions; interfacial dipole formation explains unexpected CO/O₂ behavior on 1T phase.

model_io.model: Monolayer TaSe₂ (1T and 1H phases) with adsorbates

hypotheses.hypothesis: Different adsorbates produce phase-dependent electronic modulation mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: rigid shift (K, CO, O₂ on 1T), spectral broadening (Fe on 1T), no effect (CO, O₂ on 1H)

title: Sensitivity analysis and physics-aware deep learning for aluminum mirror coatings: when network architecture outweighs loss-function design
task: Design physics-informed deep learning surrogate for aluminum mirror coating reflectance
key_results: Neural network achieves R²=0.9999 on reflectance-deficit spectrum; network architecture more crucial than loss function design; optimal design recovers smooth, opaque aluminum (91.5% reflectance); 36.5 nm reaches 91.0% reflectance
comments: Transfer-matrix validation ensures physics consistency; Debye-Waller effect causes λ⁻² scaling roughness loss; pseudo-Brewster minimum in p-polarized response.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Neural network architecture (not just loss function) is critical for metallic reflectance modeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: R²=0.9999 achieved; end-to-end surrogate-driven optimization recovers expected boundary optimum of 91.5%

title: Predicting and interpreting the irradiation-induced tensile behavior of fast reactor cladding using explainable machine learning
task: Predicting irradiation-induced tensile property changes in advanced reactor cladding steels using explainable ML
key_results: ANN MAPE 6.26±0.47% (UTS) and 10.69±0.46% (YS); YS saturation at 5–10 dpa; irradiation temperature has greater influence than dpa on YS via SHAP
comments: XGB showed best raw performance but ANN selected for continuous output and physical consistency; SHAP identifies temperature as dominant factor; 1,590 data points across 9–12Cr steels.

model_io.model: Artificial neural network for tensile property prediction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Irradiation-induced YS increase saturates at 5–10 dpa and is temperature-sensitive
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ANN predicts saturation behavior; SHAP shows irradiation temperature > dpa influence

title: Structural design and integrated tracking control simulation of a heavy duty dual axis solar tracking turntable
task: Designing a dual-axis solar tracking turntable with optical payload for cryogenic irradiance measurement
key_results: Center-of-mass offset reduced 18.4→3.8 mm; first-mode frequency increased 25.21→33.45 Hz; dual-axis RMS optical axis errors 1.505–1.539″ under full control; direct irradiance relative standard deviation reduced 4.1047%→0.0738% with full control
comments: Structural optimization and multirate control significantly reduce optical axis jitter; wind disturbance model includes three components; retrieval uncertainty 4.39% at 60 km visibility.

model_io.model: Dual-axis tracking turntable with 1 m mirror and 700 kg payload

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural optimization and integrated control reduce optical jitter to near diffraction limits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RMS errors <1.54″ achieved; full control reduces irradiance variance 55-fold

title: Unusual melting behavior of nitrogen at extreme pressures from large-scale machine-learned potential simulations
task: Predicting nitrogen phase diagram and melting curve under extreme pressure using machine-learned potentials
key_results: Unusual melting curve features cg-N/molecular-liquid/polymeric-liquid triple point and plateau; solid polymerizes before liquid ('asynchronous polymerization'); plateau onset coincides with optical reflection in experiments
comments: SCAN-trained ML potential enables ns-timescale large-scale MD; clarifies microscopic origin of controversial melting behavior; predicts triple point marking polymeric phase entry.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Solid nitrogen polymerizes before liquid under compression, creating unusual melting plateau
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: asynchronous polymerization predicts triple point; plateau onset matches experimental optical reflection onset

title: Principles of evolution guide parametrization of enzyme turnover numbers to support cellular objectives
task: Parametrize enzyme turnover numbers (kcat) in protein allocation models using evolutionary constraints
key_results: PAMparametrizer successfully recapitulated physiological phenotypes across multiple conditions in E. coli and C. glutamicum; improved metabolic behavior prediction compared to initial models despite significant variability in intracellular flux distributions
comments: The underdetermined parametrization problem highlights a fundamental challenge in systems biology: multiple parameter sets can explain the same external phenotype, limiting predictive power for internal fluxes without additional constraints.

model_io.model: Protein Allocation Model (PAM) with evolved kcat values
inputs: Experimentally observed exchange fluxes (metabolite uptake/secretion rates)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extracellular metabolite exchange rates reflect intracellular enzyme catalytic efficiencies shaped by evolution
hypotheses.result: Partial support: exchange phenotypes were recapitulated, but ensemble of solutions showed high variability in predicted intracellular fluxes

hypotheses.hypothesis: PAMparametrizer improves metabolic behavior prediction across diverse organisms
hypotheses.result: Supported for E. coli and C. glutamicum; limited validation for P. putida due to incomplete experimental data
